newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $65 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade slow at $65 -feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade was slow, with light sales at $65.00 per cwt, steady with this week's sales, but down $1.00 from late last week, feedlot sources said.
About 3,000 sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and about 6,000 sold in Kansas. Most of the week's showlists were sold or close to being sold, they said.
Temperatures were warming to the 20s (degrees Fahrenheit) from single digits the past few mornings and were expected to return to more normal readings by Saturday, sources said.
Talk circulated that packers were short on supply and picking up cattle Thursday that were bought Tuesday, some sources said.
Packers also were making sure they had enough inventory for Monday operations before scaling back going into the Christmas holiday on Wednesday, sources noted.
Demand next week was expected to be light, with at least one beef packing plant closed for maintenance and remodeling.
